subject: English
passage: One aspect of face-to-face tutoring that virtual tutoring can't replicate is the opportunity to have direct eye contact with the instructor. Does this difference matter? In an experiment, researchers had one group of students receive instruction while maintaining eye contact with their teacher, while another group received the same instruction without any eye contact. The students were then tested on how much of the material they remembered. Students who maintained eye contact with their instructor remembered significantly more information than students who had no eye contact during instruction. This finding suggests that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: students who mainly learn through virtual tutoring probably perform better on tests than students who mainly learn through face-to-face tutoring do.
choices.B: schools with both in-person and virtual programs should use identical teaching methods for both types of instruction.
choices.C: face-to-face tutoring may make educational content more memorable than it is when delivered through virtual instruction.
choices.D: virtual tutoring services may be able to improve their effectiveness by requiring students to complete more practice exercises.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The text tells us that "students who maintained eye contact with their instructor remembered significantly more information than students who had no eye contact during instruction." This suggests that being able to have direct visual interaction with an instructor in person may make educational content more memorable to a student.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The text doesn't discuss what teaching methods schools "should use," so there's not much basis for this claim. Furthermore, the study in the text suggests that in-person instruction may actually benefit from different methods, since students can maintain eye contact.
